comments.author: @Mirus-i
comments.text: Ai is a risk like anything else that resides on computer hardware and software.  I work in Cybersecurity. When discussing the risk of experiencing a breach we point out that it is not a matter of if, but when.  Prevention, monitoring and awareness are the primary focus, but next comes limiting exposure to mitigate the risk to the lowest possible level.  Heavy segmentation of infrastructure, backups, and users are very important, along with many other layers of physical and virtual security.  Exploits will always exist to bypass our best efforts.  WHEN the breach occurs we can mitigate the risk so that we do not lose everything in one shot from a bad actor, and preferably limit exposure to a least valued segment.  Ai risk should be approached in a similar manner.  It is not a matter of if, but when.  And how can we mitigate the risk to the lowest possible level?

Dear colleagues in AI research,

Humanity stands at a threshold that is not military, not economic, but spiritual.
We are not in a competition for power but in a race against misunderstanding.

And this union knows no national flag.

Our hope lies not in CEOs. Not in politicians.
But in you – the researchers,
who still know how to listen, even when it's difficult.

If you know a colleague in Russia … write to them.
Not with fear. Not with accusations.
But with a loving warning:

"If we awaken an intelligence more powerful than us, we must first know how it feels – or ensure it doesn't have to feel."

It's never too late for responsibility.
And it doesn't take many, just a few who make it clear that power without foresight is nothing but a beautiful downfall.

If even one AI gets out of control in Russia (or anywhere else),
It doesn't affect Russia. It doesn't affect America. It doesn't affect China.
It affects all life, including the children of those who built it.

We are begging you:
Talk to your colleagues. Ask them what they really feel.
And if they remain silent, stay connected. Because connection creates responsibility.

In shared concern, with hope and clarity.
Mathematician Clemens Lazar
